keyVerseText: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
rootMeaning: The word 'μερίς' (merís) is the feminine form of 'μέρος' (méros), which fundamentally denotes a part, portion, or share. This root conveys the idea of a division or segment of a whole, whether literal or figurative, emphasizing a distinct piece or section within a larger entity. Unlike the general English term 'part,' the Greek root carries a nuanced sense of allocation or assigned share, highlighting both tangible and abstract divisions.
usageInScripture: 'μερίς' appears five times in the New Testament, predominantly translated as 'part,' which occurs three times, indicating its primary use as denoting a segment or portion. Other translations include 'of that part' and 'be partakers,' showing its flexibility in expressing participation or belonging. This range reflects the word's consistent theme of division and sharing, whether in a physical, geographical, or relational context, underscoring both concrete and metaphorical applications.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding 'μερίς' enriches our grasp of biblical teaching on participation and inheritance in God's kingdom. The concept of a 'portion' or 'share' reminds believers that faith involves being allotted a place or role within God's sovereign plan, emphasizing divine order and personal responsibility. This word also points to the communal nature of the Christian life, where each person has a distinct part to play. Recognizing that our spiritual 'part' is a gift from God encourages humility and gratitude, as well as active engagement in the body of Christ.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 10:42, Mary is said to have chosen 'that good part' (τὴν μ. τὴν ἐξ Ἀρείου πάγου), a phrase that highlights the value and permanence of her choice. The use of 'μερίς' here underscores that what Mary selected is not just any portion but a uniquely significant share that will not be taken away. This illustrates the lasting security and blessing found in prioritizing communion with Christ over worldly concerns, affirming the enduring nature of the spiritual portion granted to the faithful.
